text.text: Kael to everyone who knows him. One of the best graduates of his year at the Royal Magic Academy of Nova, and a licensed mage ever since. His dream is simple: to become the number one mage in the world.
Most mages need two years to climb a class. Kael set himself one, and made it: Class 3, five months after his teacher told him to go and see the world.
The third of the four Ashveil children. Like all of them he carries two bloodlines, Shadow from his father's side and Fire from his mother's, and he chose to make Shadow his own.
A swordswoman who crossed the sea on the Morning Gull, six weeks from home. She says she is looking for someone, and not much more than that.
Kael met her the hard way: her sword drawn on Tobin in the middle of the market, sure she had seen him picking pockets. It ended in a duel, the city guard, and one shared prison cell.
Out of the cell and with nowhere else to go, she agreed to come with Kael and see the truth about Tobin for herself. Laid back, quick with her blade and quicker with a dry remark.
A cheerful prodigy of the Royal Academy, born to House Moonvale, a forgotten and sidelined family of mages.
A loyal knight commander sworn to protect the Royal Kingdom of Nova. He stands firm where others would fall.

Kael's mother, and the one who keeps the Ashveil house running while its people come and go. She writes shopping lists, counts the buns, and knows exactly which shop her son will slip into on the way home.
Born a Dracoheart, one of the great magical families of Nova. She left the clan to marry Cassius Ashveil.
Sera to her family. Kael's older sister and the second Ashveil child, a knight of the Royal Kingdom. She became a commander at twenty-three, one of the youngest ever.
Strict, and at her strictest with her little brother. Still, when Kael landed in a cell, it was Sera's word that got him out, and on Kael's word, Yuki too.
The youngest Ashveil, black-haired like Kael and, like him, drawn to Shadow. She has her brother wrapped around her finger, and she knows it.
Wants a souvenir from every town Kael visits. Wanted a midnight-blue silk ribbon first. Not navy. Midnight.
The eldest of the Ashveil children, red-haired and Fire to the bone. He chose the open sea over the court, and is rarely home.
Kael's father, one of the strongest men in the kingdom. He works for the crown, often far from home and often alone. Even his children do not know the details.
Kael's grandfather on his mother's side. Once called the Sword of Nova, now the Hero, for his part in Nova's victory over the Arulustus Empire sixteen years ago.
Kael's aunt, his mother's younger sister, and a Royal Mage of the Royal Magic Council. She once taught Fire to Kaine, Sera and Kael.

name: Isolde Wyndmere
title: Kael's Teacher
facts: Teacher at the Royal Magic Academy

text.text: One of the strongest mages of the Western Continent, and Kael's favourite teacher at the Academy. Since she retired she is rarely seen in public; when she is, the room gathers around her.
On a night walk outside the capital she showed Kael something wrong in the flow of mana, and left him with a few words: "Go, see the world. You will find that we are small."

name: Tobin
title: Carter
facts: Carts goods to and from the capital

text.text: A carter from the capital. His cart was wrecked by monsters on the Briarwood road, and Kael, sent by the Guild, found him hiding in the bushes with a twisted ankle.
Five months later, a swordswoman knocked him down in the market and called him a thief. He swears he is not.

He was lying. The night his cart was wrecked he was carrying crates for a bandit crew, and he had been picking pockets ever since to pay for the cargo he lost. He walked the bandits to the gate himself.
Tobin's wife, a few doors down from the Ashveil house. When Tobin went missing in Briarwood she filled half the Guild's request board and waited at the Main Gate from dawn.
Five months later she waited at the gate again, the night Kael and Yuki went after Tobin a second time.
Captain of the Morning Gull, which crosses the sea between the Eastern Continent and Saltwind Harbor. Six weeks at sea have not dulled her tongue.
